narrative:
The model estimated a 63.3% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt, meaning it judged failure more likely than success; because your law-school admission was tied to that forecast, the application was denied. This is a probability, not a certainty.

The strongest factor was your third-year class-standing decile of 1.0, compared with an accepted-student average of about 5.8. That weaker standing pushed the prediction most strongly toward bar-exam failure. The second strongest factor was your first-year class-standing decile, also 1.0 versus an accepted average near 6.0, again pushing toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.10 was the third most influential factor; although slightly below the accepted average of 3.23, in this prediction it acted as a relative strength and pushed toward passing, but it was not enough to outweigh the class-standing concerns.

To strengthen a future application, focus first on the academic record the prediction flagged: seek advising about the low class standing, use academic support, and document improvement. Consider retaking the LSAT if preparation can raise your score, and ask admissions how to address the forecast directly. A later application with stronger evidence of bar-exam readiness would be more persuasive.
